p.i: The commandments of Alma to his son Corianton.

chapter.li: LEChapter39 Verse1 And now, my son, I have somewhat more to say unto 2PSI thee than what I said unto 2PSI thy brother. For behold, have 2PSF ye not observed the steadiness of 2PSI thy brother? His faithfulness and his diligence in keeping the commandments of God? Behold, has he not set a good example for 2PSI thee? VerseEnd Verse2 For 2PSI thou didst not give so much heed unto my words as did 2PSI thy brother among the people of the Zoramites. Now this is what I have against 2PSI thee: 2PSI thou didst go on unto boasting in 2PSI thy strength and 2PSI thy wisdom. VerseEnd Verse3 And this is not all, my son. 2PSI Thou didst do that which was grievous unto me, for 2PSI thou didst forsake the ministry, and did go over into the land of Siron among the borders of the Lamanites after the harlot Isabel. VerseEnd Verse4 Yea, she did steal away the hearts of many, but this was no excuse for 2PSI thee, my son. 2PSI Thou shouldst have tended to the ministry wherewith 2PSI thou wast entrusted. VerseEnd Verse5 Know 2PSF ye not, my son, that these things are an abomination in the sight of the Lord, yea, most abominable above all sins, save it be the shedding of innocent blood or denying the holy ghost? VerseEnd Verse6 For behold, if 2PSF ye deny the holy ghost when it once has had place in 2PSF you, and 2PSF ye know that 2PSF ye deny it, behold, this is a sin which is unpardonable. Yea, and whosoever murdereth against the light and knowledge of God, it is not easy for him to obtain forgiveness; yea, I say unto 2PSF you, my son, that it is not easy for him to obtain a forgiveness. VerseEnd

Verse7 And now, my son, I would to God that 2PSF ye had not been guilty of so great a crime. I would not dwell upon 2PSF your crimes to harrow up 2PSF your soul if it were not for 2PSF your good. VerseEnd Verse8 But behold, 2PSF ye cannot hide 2PSF your crimes from God, and except 2PSF ye repent, they will stand as a testimony against 2PSF you at the last day. VerseEnd Verse9 Now, my son, I would that 2PSF ye should repent, and forsake 2PSF your sins, and go no more after the lusts of 2PSF your eyes, but cross yourself in all these things; for except 2PSF ye do this, 2PSF ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of God. O remember, and take it upon 2PSF you, and cross yourself in these things. VerseEnd Verse10 And I command 2PSF you to take it upon 2PSF you to counsel 2PSF your elder brothers in 2PSF your undertakings. For behold, 2PSI thou art in 2PSI thy youth, and 2PSF ye stand in need to be nourished by 2PSF your brothers and give heed to their counsel. VerseEnd Verse11 Suffer not yourself to be led away by any vain or foolish thing; suffer not that the Devil lead away 2PSF your heart again after those wicked harlots. Behold, O my son, how great iniquity 2PSF ye brought upon the Zoramites; for when they saw 2PSF your conduct, they would not believe in my words. VerseEnd Verse12 And now the spirit of the Lord doth say unto me, Command 2PSI thy children to do good, lest they lead away the hearts of many people to destruction. Therefore, I command 2PSF you, my son, in the fear of God, that 2PSF ye refrain from 2PSF your iniquities, VerseEnd Verse13 that 2PSF ye turn to the Lord with all 2PSF your mind, might, and strength, that 2PSF ye lead away the hearts of no more to do wickedly, but rather return unto them, and acknowledge 2PSF your faults, and repair that wrong which 2PSF ye have done. VerseEnd Verse14 Seek not after riches nor the vain things of this world, for behold, 2PSF you cannot carry them with 2PSF you. VerseEnd

Verse15 And now, my son, I would say somewhat unto 2PSF you concerning the coming of Christ. Behold, I say unto 2PSF you that it is he that surely shall come to take away the sins of the world; yea, he cometh to declare glad tidings of salvation unto his people. VerseEnd Verse16 And now, my son, this was the ministry unto which 2PSF ye were called: to declare these glad tidings unto this people to prepare their minds — or rather, that salvation might come unto them, that they may prepare the minds of their children to hear the word at the time of his coming. VerseEnd Verse17 And now I will ease 2PSF your mind somewhat on this subject. Behold, 2PSF you marvel why these things should be known so long beforehand. Behold, I say unto 2PSF you, is not a soul at this time as precious unto God as a soul will be at the time of his coming? VerseEnd Verse18 Is it not as necessary that the plan of redemption should be made known unto this people as well as unto their children? VerseEnd Verse19 Is it not as easy at this time for the Lord to send his angel to declare those glad tidings unto us as unto our children, or as after the time of his coming? VerseEnd

LEChapter40 Verse1 Now, my son, here is somewhat more I would say unto 2PSI thee, for I perceive that 2PSI thy mind is worried concerning the resurrection of the dead. VerseEnd Verse2 Behold, I say unto 2PSF you that there is no resurrection — or I would say in other words that this mortal does not put on immortality, this corruption does not put on incorruption — until after the coming of Christ. VerseEnd Verse3 Behold, he bringeth to pass the resurrection of the dead. But behold, my son, the resurrection is not yet. Now I unfold unto 2PSF you a mystery; nevertheless, there are many mysteries which are kept, that no one knoweth them save God himself. But I shew unto 2PSF you one thing which I have inquired diligently of God that I might know, that is concerning the resurrection. VerseEnd Verse4 Behold, there is a time appointed that all shall come forth from the dead. Now when this time cometh, no one knows, but God knoweth the time which is appointed. VerseEnd Verse5 Now whether there shall be one time, or a second time, or a third time that men shall come forth from the dead, it mattereth not, for God knoweth all these things. And it sufficeth me to know that this is the case — that there is a time appointed when all shall rise from the dead. VerseEnd

Verse6 And now there must needs be a space betwixt the time of death and the time of the resurrection. VerseEnd Verse7 And now I would inquire, what becometh of the souls of men from this time of death to the time appointed for the resurrection? VerseEnd Verse8 Now whether there is more than one time appointed for men to rise, it mattereth not, for all do not die at once, and this mattereth not — all is as one day with God, and time only is measured unto man. VerseEnd Verse9 Therefore, there is a time appointed unto men that they shall rise from the dead, and there is a space between the time of death and the resurrection.

And now, concerning this space of time, what becometh of the souls of men is the thing which I have inquired diligently of the Lord to know; and this is the thing of which I do know. VerseEnd Verse10 And when the time cometh when all shall rise, then shall they know that God knoweth all the times which are appointed unto man. VerseEnd Verse11 Now concerning the state of the soul between death and the resurrection, behold, it has been made known unto me by an angel that the spirits of all men, as soon as they are departed from this mortal body, yea, the spirits of all men, whether they be good or evil, are taken home to that God who gave them life. VerseEnd Verse12 And then shall it come to pass that the spirits of those who are righteous are received into a state of happiness, which is called paradise — a state of rest, a state of peace where they shall rest from all their troubles, and from all care and sorrow, etc. VerseEnd Verse13 And then shall it come to pass that the spirits of the wicked, yea, who are evil — for behold, they have no part nor portion of the spirit of the Lord; for behold, they chose evil works rather than good, therefore the spirit of the Devil did enter into them and take possession of their house — and these shall be cast out into outer darkness. There shall be weeping, and wailing, and gnashing of teeth, and this because of their own iniquity, being led captive by the will of the Devil. VerseEnd Verse14 Now this is the state of the souls of the wicked, yea, in darkness and a state of awful, fearful looking for, of the fiery indignation of the wrath of God upon them. Thus they remain in this state, as well as the righteous in paradise, until the time of their resurrection. VerseEnd

Verse15 Now there are some that have understood that this state of happiness and this state of misery of the soul, before the resurrection, was a first resurrection. Yea, I admit it may be termed a resurrection, the raising the spirit or the soul and their consignation to happiness or misery according to the words which have been spoken. VerseEnd Verse16 And behold, again it hath been spoken that there is a first resurrection, a resurrection of all those who have been, or who are, or who shall be, down to the resurrection of Christ from the dead. VerseEnd Verse17 Now we do not suppose that this first resurrection, which is spoken of in this manner, can be the resurrection of the souls and their consignation to happiness or misery. 2PSF Ye cannot suppose that this is what it meaneth. VerseEnd Verse18 Behold, I say unto 2PSF you, nay, but it meaneth the reuniting of the soul with the body, of those from the days of Adam down to the resurrection of Christ. VerseEnd Verse19 Now whether the souls and the bodies of those of whom have been spoken shall all be reunited at once, the wicked as well as the righteous, I do not say. Let it suffice that I say that they all come forth, or in other words, that their resurrection cometh to pass before the resurrection of those who die after the resurrection of Christ. VerseEnd Verse20 Now, my son, I do not say that their resurrection cometh at the resurrection of Christ, but behold, I give it as my opinion that the souls and the bodies are reunited of the righteous, at the resurrection of Christ and his ascension into Heaven. VerseEnd Verse21 But whether it be at his resurrection or after, I do not say.

But this much I say, that there is a space between death and the resurrection of the body, and a state of the soul, in happiness or in misery, until the time which is appointed of God that the dead shall come forth and be reunited, both soul and body, and be brought to stand before God and be judged according to their works. VerseEnd Verse22 Yea, this bringeth about the restoration of those things of which have been spoken by the mouths of the prophets — VerseEnd Verse23 the soul shall be restored to the body and the body to the soul; yea, and every limb and joint shall be restored to its body, yea, even a hair of their heads shall not be lost, but all things shall be restored to their proper and perfect frame. VerseEnd Verse24 And now, my son, this is the restoration of which has been spoken by the mouths of the prophets. VerseEnd Verse25 And then shall the righteous shine forth in the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse26 But behold, an awful death cometh upon the wicked, for they die as to things pertaining to things of righteousness, for they are unclean, and no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of God. But they are cast out, and consigned to partake of the fruits of their labors, or their works, which have been evil; and they drink the dregs of a bitter cup. VerseEnd

LEChapter41 Verse1 And now, my son, I have somewhat to say concerning the restoration of which has been spoken. For behold, some have wrested the scriptures and have gone far astray because of this thing, and I perceive that 2PSI thy mind has been worried also concerning this thing. But behold, I will explain it unto 2PSI thee. VerseEnd Verse2 I say unto 2PSI thee, my son, that the plan of restoration is requisite with the justice of God, for it is requisite that all things should be restored to their proper order. Behold, it is requisite and just, according to the power and resurrection of Christ, that the soul of man should be restored to its body, and that every part of the body should be restored to itself. VerseEnd Verse3 And it is also requisite with the justice of God that men should be judged according to their works. And if their works were good in this life and the desires of their hearts were good, that they should also, at the last day, be restored unto that which is good; VerseEnd Verse4 and if his works are evil, they shall be restored unto him for evil. Therefore, all things shall be restored to its proper order, everything to its natural frame: mortality raised to immortality, corruption to incorruption, raised to endless happiness to inherit the kingdom of God, or to endless misery to inherit the kingdom of the Devil, the one on one hand, the other on the other, VerseEnd Verse5 the one restored to happiness according to his desires of happiness, or to good according to his desires of good, and the other to evil according to his desires of evil. For as he has desired to do evil all the day long, even so shall he have his reward of evil when the night cometh. VerseEnd Verse6 And so it is on the other hand: if he hath repented of his sins and desired righteousness until the end of his days, even so shall he be rewarded unto righteousness. VerseEnd Verse7 These are they that are redeemed of the Lord, yea, these are they that are taken out, that are delivered from that endless night of darkness. And thus they stand or fall. For behold, they are their own judges, whether to do good or do evil. VerseEnd Verse8 Now the decrees of God are unalterable. Therefore, the way is prepared that whosoever will may walk therein and be saved. VerseEnd

Verse9 And now behold, my son, do not risk one more offense against 2PSF your God upon those points of doctrine which 2PSF ye have hitherto risked to commit sin. VerseEnd Verse10 Do not suppose because that it has been spoken concerning restoration that 2PSF ye shall be restored from sin to happiness. Behold, I say unto 2PSF you, wickedness never was happiness. VerseEnd Verse11 And now, my son, all men that are in a state of nature — or I would say, in a carnal state — are in the gall of bitterness and in the bonds of iniquity. They are without God in the world and they have gone contrary to the nature of God, therefore they are in a state contrary to the nature of happiness. VerseEnd

Verse12 And now behold, is the meaning of the word restoration to take a thing of a natural state and place it in an unnatural state? Or to place it in a state opposite to its nature? VerseEnd Verse13 O, my son, this is not the case, but the meaning of the word restoration is to bring back again evil for evil, or carnal for carnal, or devilish for devilish; good for that which is good, righteous for that which is righteous, just for that which is just, merciful for that which is merciful. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore, my son, see that 2PSF ye are merciful unto 2PSF your brethren. Deal justly, judge righteously, and do good continually; and if 2PSF ye do all these things, then shall 2PSF ye receive 2PSF your reward. Yea, 2PSF ye shall have mercy restored unto 2PSF you again, 2PSF ye shall have justice restored unto 2PSF you again, 2PSF ye shall have a righteous judgment restored unto 2PSF you again, and 2PSF ye shall have good rewarded unto 2PSF you again. VerseEnd Verse15 For that which 2PSF ye do send out shall return unto 2PSF you again and be restored. Therefore, the word restoration more fully condemneth the sinner and justifieth him not at all. VerseEnd

LEChapter42 Verse1 And now, my son, I perceive there is somewhat more which doth worry 2PSF your mind, which 2PSF ye cannot understand, which is concerning the justice of God in the punishment of the sinner; for 2PSF ye do try to suppose that it is injustice that the sinner should be consigned to a state of misery. VerseEnd Verse2 Now behold, my son, I will explain this thing unto 2PSI thee. For behold, after the Lord God sent our first parents forth from the Garden of Eden to till the ground from whence they were taken, yea, he drove out the man, and he placed at the east end of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword, which turned every way to keep the tree of life. VerseEnd Verse3 Now we see that the man had become as God, knowing good and evil, and lest he should put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever, that the Lord God placed cherubim and the flaming sword, that he should not partake of the fruit. VerseEnd Verse4 And thus we see that there was a time granted unto man to repent, yea, a probationary time, a time to repent and serve God. VerseEnd Verse5 For behold, if Adam had put forth his hand immediately and partook of the tree of life, he would have lived for ever, according to the word of God, having no space for repentance. Yea, and also the word of God would have been void and the great plan of salvation would have been frustrated. VerseEnd Verse6 But behold, it was appointed unto man to die. Therefore, as they were cut off from the tree of life, they should be cut off from the face of the earth, and man became lost for ever; yea, they became fallen man. VerseEnd

Verse7 And now we see by this that our first parents were cut off, both temporally and spiritually, from the presence of the Lord; and thus we see they became subjects to follow after their own will. VerseEnd Verse8 Now behold, it was not expedient that man should be reclaimed from this temporal death, for that would destroy the great plan of happiness. VerseEnd Verse9 Therefore, as the soul could never die and the Fall had brought upon all mankind a spiritual death as well as a temporal (that is, they were cut off from the presence of the Lord), therefore it was expedient that mankind should be reclaimed from this spiritual death. VerseEnd Verse10 Therefore, as they had become carnal, sensual, and devilish by nature, this probationary state became a state for them to prepare; it became a preparatory state. VerseEnd

Verse11 And now remember, my son, if it were not for the plan of redemption (laying it aside), as soon as they were dead, their souls were miserable, being cut off from the presence of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse12 And now there was no means to reclaim men from this fallen state, which man had brought upon himself because of his own disobedience. VerseEnd Verse13 Therefore, according to justice, the plan of redemption could not be brought about — only on conditions of repentance of men in this probationary state, yea, this preparatory state. For except it were for these conditions, mercy could not take effect except it should destroy the work of justice. Now the work of justice could not be destroyed; if so, God would cease to be God. VerseEnd Verse14 And thus we see that all mankind were fallen, and they were in the grasp of justice, yea, the justice of God, which consigned them for ever to be cut off from his presence. VerseEnd Verse15 And now the plan of mercy could not be brought about except an atonement should be made. Therefore, God himself atoneth for the sins of the world, to bring about the plan of mercy, to appease the demands of justice, that God might be a perfect, just God, and a merciful God also. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now repentance could not come unto men except there were a punishment, which also was as eternal as the life of the soul, should be affixed opposite to the plan of happiness, which was as eternal also as the life of the soul. VerseEnd Verse17 Now, how could a man repent except he should sin? How could he sin if there was no law? How could there be a law save there was a punishment? VerseEnd Verse18 Now there was a punishment affixed and a just law given, which brought remorse of conscience unto man. VerseEnd Verse19 Now if there was no law given (if a man murdered, he should die), would he be afraid he should die if he should murder? VerseEnd Verse20 And also, if there was no law given against sin, men would not be afraid to sin. VerseEnd Verse21 And if there was no law given if men sinned, what could justice do? Or mercy either? For they would have no claim upon the creature. VerseEnd Verse22 But there is a law given, and a punishment affixed, and repentance granted, which repentance mercy claimeth. Otherwise, justice claimeth the creature and executeth the law, and the law inflicteth the punishment. If not so, the works of justice would be destroyed and God would cease to be God. VerseEnd Verse23 But God ceaseth not to be God, and mercy claimeth the penitent, and mercy cometh because of the atonement, and the atonement bringeth to pass the resurrection of the dead, and the resurrection of the dead bringeth back men into the presence of God. And thus they are restored into his presence, to be judged according to their works, according to the law and justice. VerseEnd Verse24 For behold, justice exerciseth all his demands, and also mercy claimeth all which is her own; and thus none but the truly penitent are saved. VerseEnd

Verse25 What? Do 2PSF ye suppose that mercy can rob justice? I say unto 2PSF you, nay, not one whit. If so, God would cease to be God. VerseEnd Verse26 And thus God bringeth about his great and eternal purposes, which were prepared from the foundation of the world. And thus cometh about the salvation and the redemption of men, and also their destruction and misery. VerseEnd Verse27 Therefore, O my son, whosoever will come may come and partake of the waters of life freely. And whosoever will not come, the same is not compelled to come, but in the last day it shall be restored unto him according to his deeds. VerseEnd Verse28 If he has desired to do evil and has not repented in his days, behold, evil shall be done unto him according to the restoration of God. VerseEnd

Verse29 And now, my son, I desire that 2PSF ye should let these things trouble 2PSF you no more, and only let 2PSF your sins trouble 2PSF you with that trouble which shall bring 2PSF you down unto repentance. VerseEnd Verse30 O my son, I desire that 2PSF ye should deny the justice of God no more. Do not endeavor to excuse yourself in the least point because of 2PSF your sins by denying the justice of God, but do 2PSF you let the justice of God and his mercy, and his long-suffering, have full sway in 2PSF your heart, but let it bring 2PSF you down to the dust in humility. VerseEnd Verse31 And now, my son, 2PSF ye are called of God to preach the word unto this people. And now, my son, go 2PSI thy way; declare the word with truth and soberness, that 2PSI thou mayest bring souls unto repentance, that the great plan of mercy may have claim upon them. And may God grant unto 2PSF you, yea, even according to my words. Amen. VerseEnd
